the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي هذا﴾ ذا is a demonstrative; the two are attached to the omitted fronted khabar of إن. ﴿لَبَلاغاً﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and بلاغا is the postponed noun of إن. ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ the two are attached to بلاغا. ﴿عابِدِينَ﴾ a naʿt of قوم, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and ما is negating. ﴿أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ the two are attached to رحمة. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ the two are attached to يوحى. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining and the restrained. ﴿إِلهُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾ a naʿt of إله; the clause أنما إلهكم إله is, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يوحى. [Translator's note: the source heads this word ﴿إِنَّما﴾, but the verse reads ﴿أَنَّما﴾, as its own analysis (أنما … in the position of nāʾib fāʿil) assumes.] ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; هل is an interrogative particle. ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:109-112.t: ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, which was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿آذَنْتُكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿عَلى سَواءٍ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) آذنتكم. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and إن is a particle of negation. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, its fāʿil latent; the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَقَرِيبٌ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿قَرِيبٌ﴾ fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿بَعِيدٌ﴾ conjoined to قريب. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl of أدري. [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is ordinarily described as the object of أدري, whose operation is suspended.] ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ إن and its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْجَهْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar. ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl from الجهر. ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and إن is negating. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ لعل, its noun and its khabar. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to فتنة or to a naʿt (adjective) of it. ﴿وَمَتاعٌ﴾ conjoined to فتنة. ﴿إِلى حِينٍ﴾ the two are attached to متاع; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of أدري. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; it is annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿احْكُمْ﴾ a verb of supplication, its fāʿil omitted. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to احكم. ﴿وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمنُ الْمُسْتَعانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by على, and the two are attached to المستعان. ﴿تَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ مُّحْدَثٍ﴾: had al-muḥdath been accusative or nominative, it would have been correct. The accusative would be by the verb: "there does not come to them, newly revealed…"; the nominative would be by referring back to the underlying sense of al-dhikr, because if you dropped (مِن) you would put al-dhikr in the nominative. It is like your saying: "mā min aḥadin qāʾimin", "qāʾimun" and "qāʾiman" ("there is no one standing"). The accusative in this [Translator's note: last example] rests on the acceptability of the bāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. as with mā… bi-qāʾimin, as transmitted], and in the first on the verb.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ is accusative by conjunction with His saying ﴿وهم يلعبونَ﴾, because His saying "while they play" is on a par with "playing" (lāʿibīna); so it is as if: "except that they listen to it playing, their hearts distracted." Its accusative may also be by deriving it from the pronoun implied in (يلعبُون): they play thus, their hearts distracted. Had you put (لاهية) in the nominative, making it follow yalʿabūna, it would have been correct, as you say: "ʿAbd Allāh is amusing himself (yalhū) and playing (lāʿibun)." Similar to it is the poet's saying:
* يَقْصِدُ فى أَسْوُقها وجائر *
(He aims straight at their shanks, and he is erring.)
It may also be nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), not by referring back to yalʿabūna.
His saying ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَى﴾: it was said wa-asarrū only because it refers to "the people" (al-nās), who were described with amusement and play; and (الذينَ) follows al-nās and is genitive, as though you had said: "Drawn near for the people whose state is this." If you wish, you make (الذين) a new beginning, nominative, as though you made it an explanation of the nouns [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun] in asarrū, as He said ﴿فَعَمُوا وصَمُّوا ثمَّ تَابَ اللهُ عليهم ثم عَمُوا وصَمُّوا كثير منهم.﴾

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّي﴾ and ﴿قُل ربّى﴾: all is correct.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلاَمٍ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ﴾: it is turned with bal on the sense of their denial, even though the speech expressing their denial has not appeared before it, because its meaning is an address to, and a report about, the deniers.
His saying: ﴿فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِآيَةٍ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلأَوَّلُونَ﴾: like the signs which the former ones brought.

farraa:6-6.t: So Allah said ﴿مَآ آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَآ﴾, of those to whom a sign came; so how should these believe?

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿فَاسْئَلُوۤاْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾: that is, the people of the books, the Torah and the Gospel.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَداً لاَّ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾: He made jasad singular and did not pluralize it — and that is good Arabic — because jasad is like your saying "an embodied thing", since it is derived from a verb, so it suffices for the plural; likewise the reading of whoever read ﴿لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سَقْفاً من فِضَّةٍ﴾, the meaning being "roofs". Then He said ﴿لا يأكلونَ الطعَام﴾: He is saying: We made them bodies only so that they would eat food, ﴿وَمَا كانوا خالدينَ﴾ by their eating and drinking — meaning the men who were sent [116 a]. Had it been said "lā yaʾkulu al-ṭaʿām" (singular), it would have been correct, making the verb belong to al-jasad, just as you say: "You two are two righteous things", and "a righteous thing", and "a thing, two righteous ones" [Translator's note: so in the text]. Similar to it is ﴿أَمَنةً نُعَاساً تَغْشَى طائِفَةً﴾ and ﴿يَغْشَى﴾; and similar to it is ﴿إنَّ شَجَرةَ الزقُّومِ طَعَامُ الأثيمِ﴾ — He said ﴿كَالمُهْلِ تَغْلِى﴾ with reference to the tree, and (يَغْلِى) with reference to the food; and likewise His saying ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنْىّ يُمْنَى﴾ and tumnā.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿كِتَاباً فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ﴾: your honour.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿إِذَا هُمْ مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ﴾: they flee and are routed.

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَا زَالَت تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ means their saying "We have indeed been wrongdoers", i.e. they kept on repeating it. In this place the masculine would also be suitable; it is like His saying ﴿ذَلَكَ مِنْ أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الغَيْبِ﴾.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْواً﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-lahw is "child" in the dialect of Ḥaḍramawt.
His saying: ﴿إِن كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: "We were not doers [Translator's note: of that]." (إنْ) may have the meaning of (ما), as in His saying ﴿إنْ أَنْتَ إلاّ نَذِيرٌ﴾. And it may be the in that has the role of a condition (jazāʾ), so it would be: "if We were doers — and We do not do it." That is the closer of the two ways to the approach of Arabic, and Allah knows best.

farraa:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾: illā in this place is on a par with siwā ("other than"), as though you said: "Were there gods in them other than (or besides) Allah, their inhabitants would have been ruined" (meaning the inhabitants of heaven and earth).

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُّكْرَمُونَ﴾: its meaning is "rather, they are honoured servants". Had it been "bal ʿibādan mukramīna" (accusative), referred back to al-walad, i.e. "We did not take them as a child, but We took them as honoured servants", (it would have been correct).

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقاً فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾: the sky was split open with rain and the earth with vegetation. (He said) (كَانَتَا رَتْقاً) and did not say ratqayn (dual); (it is) as He said ﴿مهما جَعَلناهم جَسَداً﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse (21:8) reads «وما جعلناهم جسدا»].
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ is genitive. Had it been ḥayyan (accusative), it would have been correct, i.e. "We made everything living from water."

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفاً مَّحْفُوظاً﴾: had it been said maḥfūẓatan, the feminine would refer to al-samāʾ and the masculine to al-saqf, as He said ﴿أَمَنَةً نُعَاساً تَغْشَى﴾ and (يَغْشَى). And it was called (a roof) though it is heavens because it is a roof over the earth like the roof over a house. The meaning of His saying (مَّحْفُوظاً): it is guarded (from the devils) by the stars.
His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾: its signs are its moon, its sun and its stars. Mujāhid read (وهم عن آياتِها مُعْرِضونَ) [Translator's note: the source prints the plural here; the following words indicate that Mujāhid's reading was the singular «آيتها»], making it singular (and making) the sky with what is in it a single sign. All is correct.

farraa:33-33.t: And He said: ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ for non-humans — for the sun, the moon, the night and the day. That is because swimming is among the acts of humans, so it was said with the nūn [Translator's note: of the masculine rational plural], just as it was said ﴿والشمسَ والقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَاجِدِين﴾, because prostration is among the acts of humans. It is said that al-falak is a restrained wave in which they run.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَالِدُونَ﴾: the fāʾ has entered the condition — which is (إن) — and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the condition is connected to Qurʾān before it; so the alif of interrogation was placed in it before the fāʾ of the condition. The fāʾ entered His saying (فهم) because it is the apodosis of the condition. Had the fāʾ been dropped from His saying (فهم), it would have been correct for two reasons. One of them is that you intend the fāʾ and imply it, because it does not change (هم) from its nominative; in such a place implication is suitable. The other reason is that (هم) is meant to be brought forward to the fāʾ, so it is as though [116 b] it were said: "Will they be the immortals if you die?"

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾: had you given tanwīn to (ذائقة) and put (الموت) in the accusative, it would have been correct. What the Arabs mostly choose is tanwīn and the accusative for the future; when its meaning is past, they hardly say it other than with the construct (iḍāfa). As for the future, it is your saying "anā ṣāʾimun yawma al-khamīs" ("I am fasting on Thursday") when it is a coming Thursday; if you report the fast of a past Thursday, you say "anā ṣāʾimu yawmi al-khamīs". This is the way of governing (al-ʿamal). They also choose tanwīn when it comes with negation; of that is their saying "mā huwa bi-tārikin ḥaqqahu" and "huwa ghayru tārikin ḥaqqahu" ("he is not one to give up his right"); they hardly ever omit the tanwīn [Translator's note: there]. Yet omitting it is common and permissible, and they recite the saying of Abū al-Aswad:
فألفَيْتُه غير مستعتب * ولا ذاكرِ اللهَ إلا قليلاَ
(I found him not seeking to make amends, nor remembering Allah except a little.)
Whoever drops the nūn and uses the accusative says: the intention is tanwīn with negation, but I dropped the nūn because of the quiescent letter it met, while giving it its governing force. Whoever uses the genitive has made it a construct (iḍāfa).

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿أَهَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾: He means: who disparages your gods. Likewise His saying ﴿سَمِعْنَا فَتَى يَذْكُرُهم يُقَالُ لَهُ إبراهِيمُ﴾, i.e. disparages them. You say to a man: "If you mention me, you will surely regret it", while you mean: with ill. ʿAntara said:
لا تذكرى مُهْرِى وَمَا أطعمتُهُ * فيكونَ جِلْدكِ مثل جِلد الأشهبِ
(Do not mention my colt and what I have fed him, lest your skin become like the skin of the grey horse.)
That is, do not reproach me for preferring my colt; so he made dhikr mean reproach.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿خُلِقَ ٱلإنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾, and "ʿalā ʿajal": it is as though you said: "I built him and created him out of haste and upon haste."

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَـٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ﴾: (مَتَي) is in the position of the accusative, because if you made its answer overt you would see it in the accusative and say: "The promise is on such-and-such a day (yawma)." (And if) you made (متى) be in the position of the nominative, as you say "When is the appointment?" and he says "yawmu al-khamīs" or "yawma al-khamīs" [Translator's note: both are possible]. Allah said ﴿مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ﴾; had you used the accusative, it would have been correct. When you make the appointment an indefinite of days, nights, months and years, you use the nominative and say [Translator's note: the text has «فلقت», evidently for «فقلت»]: "Your appointment is a day or two days, a night or two nights", as Allah said ﴿غُدُوُّهَا شَهْرٌ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهْرٌ﴾. The Arabs say: "The cold is only two months" and "the summer is only two months"; had it come in the accusative, it would have been correct. They chose the nominative only because you have left the two months unspecified, so the two together became as it were a time-span for the summer. They chose the accusative with the definite only because it is a known time, assigned to what follows it, so the adverbial (al-ṣifa) is good — just as you say "ʿAbd Allāh is a dūnun among men" (nominative, "inferior"), and "ʿAbd Allāh is dūnaka" (below you), using the accusative. Similar to it: "The two armies met; the Muslims were a side (jānibun) and the unbelievers a side." When you add a genitive you use the accusative and say: "The Muslims were on the side of (jāniba) their companion, and the unbelievers on the side of their companion." When you do not put jānib in construct, you make them themselves like the side, not that they are in it. Make analogies on this basis.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ﴾, and His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنِى مِنَ الله إن عَصَيْتُه﴾: "who will protect me?" That is its meaning — and Allah knows best — throughout the Qurʾān.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم﴾
is hamzated. (If) you dropped [117 a] the hamza of something like it outside the Qurʾān, you would say yaklūkum with a quiescent wāw, or yaklākum with a quiescent alif, like yakhshākum. Whoever makes it a quiescent wāw says kalān [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps «كَلاَت» is meant] with alif, dropping the glottal stop (al-nabra) from it; and whoever says yaklākum says kalaytu, like qaḍaytu; that is of the dialect of Quraysh. All is good, except that in both ways they say maklūwa without hamza, and maklūw without hamza is more frequent than their saying makliyya. Had makliyy been said in the dialect of those who say kalaytu, it would have been correct. I heard one of the Arabs recite the saying of al-Farazdaq:
وما خاصم الاقوامَ مِن ذى خُصُومةٍ * كَورْهاء مَشْنِىّ إليها حَليلُها
(No disputant ever disputed with people like a foolish woman whose husband is hated by her.)
So he built it on shanītu, dropping the glottal stop. His saying ﴿مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾: He means "from the command of the Most Merciful"; "command" has been omitted while it is meant, as He said in another place ﴿فَمَنْ يَنْصُرنِى مِنَ اللهِ﴾, meaning: who will protect me from the punishment of Allah? And He made the meaning overt in another place, saying ﴿فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنَا مِنْ بَأْسِ اللهِ إِنْ جَاءنَا﴾.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ means the gods: they cannot protect themselves. ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ means the unbelievers, i.e. they are not given protection (and they [Translator's note: the gods] are not protected from Us). Do you not see that the Arabs say "(He was a protector (jār) to us)", meaning: he grants you protection and defends you? So He said (يُصْحَبُونَ) in the sense of granting protection [Translator's note: the text has «بالإجازة»; «بالإجارة», "protection", is evidently meant].

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ﴾: you put (الصُمّ) in the nominative because the act is theirs. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (وَلاَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعَاءَ), putting (الصم) in the accusative because the act falls upon it.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَازِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ﴾: al-qisṭ is a description of the scales even though it is singular; it is on a par with your saying to a group: "You are contentment and justice." Likewise al-ḥaqq: when it describes one, two or more, it remains singular.
His saying: ﴿لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾: and "on the Day of Resurrection".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾: it refers to al-ḥabba ("the grain"); had it been atainā bihi, (it would have been correct) because mithqāl is masculine. Had al-mithqāl been put in the nominative, as He said ﴿وإنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَة فَنِظرةٌ﴾, it would have been correct. Mujāhid read (آتَيْنَا بهَا) with a long alif, meaning: "We requited for it", on the pattern fāʿalnā; that is a good option.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءً﴾: it is a description of al-furqān, and its meaning — and Allah knows best — is "We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion as a light and a reminder"; the wāw entered as He said ﴿إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الكوَاكِب وَحِفْظاً﴾, i.e. "We made that"; and likewise (and a light and a reminder): "We gave that."

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ﴾: al-mubārak is nominative as a description of al-dhikr. Had it been accusative, as in your saying "We sent it down blessed", it would have been correct.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ رُشْدَهُ﴾: his guidance, when he was in the underground hiding-place, until Allah brought him to what He brought him. Similar to it is ﴿وَلَوْ شئنا لآتَيْنَا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُدَاهَا﴾: its right guidance.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَٱللَّهِ لأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾: they had wanted to go out to a festival of theirs, and Abraham excused himself from them and stayed behind (and said): "I am ill." When they had gone, he smashed their gods except the biggest of them. When they returned, one of them said: "I heard Abraham say: By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols." That is His saying ﴿سَمِعْنَا فَتيً يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَال لَهُ إبراهيم﴾: he mentions them with disparagement (and abuse), and with what he said about plotting.

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَاذاً﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it (جِذَاذاً), and the reading of the people otherwise [117 b] is (جُذَاذاً) with ḍamma. Whoever says (جُذَاذاً), giving the jīm ḍamma, it is a singular, like al-ḥuṭām and al-rufāt ("debris", "crumbled remains"). Whoever says (جِذَاذاً) with kasra, it is a plural, as though it were jadhīdh and jidhādh, like khafīf and khifāf.

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾: in front of everyone. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ against him with what the one person testified to. And it is said: perhaps they will witness his affair and what is done to him.

farraa:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَـٰذَا﴾: some people said "bal faʿallahu kabīruhum", with the doubled consonant, meaning "fa-laʿallahu kabīruhum" ("perhaps it was their biggest one"). Some people said: "Rather, their biggest one did it, if they can speak", making the act of the biggest one dependent on "if they can speak", while they cannot speak. The approach that the generality follow is "bal faʿalahu", just as Joseph said ﴿أَيَّتُها العِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ﴾, while they had not stolen. Allah has supported His prophets with more than this.

farraa:65-65.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾: He is saying: they turned back when they recognized Abraham's argument, and said: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ يَنطِقُونَ﴾. (Knowing and thinking are on a par with an oath; for that reason ʿalima is met with mā) — so He said: ﴿عَلِمْتَ مَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾, like one's saying: "By Allah, you are not our brother"; and likewise His saying: ﴿وظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾.
Had the Arabs put (أنْ) before (ما), so that it was said "ʿalimtu an mā fīka khayr" and "ẓanantu an mā fīka khayr", it would have been correct. But when one of these verbs meets a particle such as (إن) accompanied by the lām, or an interrogative — as in your saying "Find out for me: did ʿAbd Allāh stand or Zayd?" — (or la-in) or law, they make do with that particle and do not put (أَنْ) before it. Do you not see His saying ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾? Had it been said "an la-yasjununnahu", it would have been correct, as the poet said:
وخبَّرتما أن إنمَّا بين بيشَةٍ * ونَجْرانَ أَحوى والمحلُّ خَصيب
(And you two told me that between Bīsha and Najrān it is dark green with pasture, and the camping-ground is fertile.)
He put an before innamā; for that reason we have allowed its entry before the rest of the particles I have described to you.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً﴾: al-nāfila ("the extra gift") refers to Jacob specifically, because he is a grandson; that is how it has reached me.

farraa:74-74.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلُوطاً آتَيْنَاهُ﴾: Lūṭ is accusative by the hāʾ in ﴿آتَيْنَاه﴾ that refers back to him. The other accusative is by implying ﴿واذكر لوطا﴾ ("and mention Lot") or ﴿ولقد أرسلنا﴾ ("and We sent"), or whatever is mentioned at the beginning of the sūra; and even if it is not mentioned, the implied element is only from [Translator's note: the notion of] the sending or of the mentioning. Similar to it is ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ﴾: (الريح) is accusative by an implied verb whose meaning is known: either "We subjected" or "We gave him".
Likewise His saying: ﴿ونُوحاً إذ نَادَى﴾ is by the implied [Translator's note: verb of] mentioning.
His saying: ﴿وَدَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمان﴾ — and all [Translator's note: the text has «وجمع», evidently for «وجميع»] the mentions of the prophets that come to you in this sūra — you put them in the accusative by coordination (nasaq) with what is accusative by the implied [Translator's note: verb of] mentioning.

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾: al-nafsh is [Translator's note: grazing] by night. They were sheep belonging to a people that got into the vineyard of others. They brought their case to David, and he judged that the owners of the vineyard should have the sheep, and the vineyard be handed to the owners of the sheep. That reached his son Solomon, who said: "Something other than this would have been kinder to both parties." So David [Translator's note: the text has «دواد» for «داود»] adjured him to give judgement. He said: "I think the sheep should be handed to the owners of the vineyard, who will benefit from their milk, their young and their wool, and the vineyard handed to the owners of the sheep [118 a], who will tend it until it returns to its state on the day it was spoiled." It is related that the two values in this judgement [Translator's note: the text has «الحم», evidently for «الحكم»] were equal: the value of what they obtained from the sheep and the value of what the sheep had spoiled of the vineyard. That is His saying: ﴿فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ﴾. And His saying: ﴿وَكُنَّا لحكمِهم﴾.
In one reading: (وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمَهِمَا شاهِدِين), and it is like His saying: ﴿فَإنْ كَانَ لَهُ إخْوَةٌ﴾, meaning two brothers or more. This is like His saying: ﴿لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ﴾, since He used the plural for two.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ﴾, and (ليُحْصِنَكم) and (لنُحْصِنكم): whoever says (ليُحصنكم) with yāʾ does so because labūs is masculine; whoever says (لِتُحْصنكم) with tāʾ takes it to refer to ṣanʿa, which is feminine — or, if you wish, you make it feminine because of the coats of mail (al-durūʿ), since they are the labūs. Whoever reads (لنُحصنكم) with nūn is saying: "so that We may protect you". In this sense (ليُحصنكم) with yāʾ is also permissible: "so that Allah may protect you from your violence".

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: it used to run with Solomon to every place, then return with him the same day to his dwelling. That is His saying ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

farraa:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلاً دُونَ ذٰلِكَ﴾: apart from the diving; He means other than diving: building.
His saying: ﴿وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ﴾: for the devils. That is because they were kept from spoiling what they made. When one of the devils had finished his work, Solomon would assign him to another work, because when he finished what he was making and had no occupation, he would turn to demolishing what he had built. That is His saying: ﴿وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ﴾.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَّعَهُمْ﴾: it is related that Job had seven sons and seven daughters, and they died during his affliction. When Allah removed it from him, Allah brought his sons and daughters back to life for him, and the like of them was born to him after that. That is His saying ﴿أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً﴾: We did that as a mercy.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: He means that We would not decree for him the punishment that We decreed.
His saying: ﴿فَنَادَىٰ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ أَن لاَّ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ أَنتَ﴾: it is said: the darkness of the sea, and of the belly of the whale and its bowels (miʿā, with the short final vowel) in which Jonah was; those are the darknesses.

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُنجِـي ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: the readers read it with two nūns, while its written form has one nūn. That is because the first nūn is vowelled and the second quiescent, and the quiescent one does not show in pronunciation; since it was hidden, it was dropped [Translator's note: in writing].
ʿĀṣim — as far as I know — read (نُجِّى) with one nūn and put (المؤمنين) in the accusative, as though he tolerated a grammatical error (laḥn); we know no explanation for it other than this: that a verb whose agent is not named, when it has a noun to itself, puts it in the nominative — unless the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied in nujjiya, intended as the nominative, and (المؤمنين) put in the accusative. Then it would be like your saying "ḍuriba al-ḍarbu Zaydan" ("the beating was beaten Zayd"); then you refer to the beating by a pronoun and say "ḍuriba Zaydan". Likewise "nujjiya al-najāʾu al-muʾminīna".

farraa:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ﴾: He is saying: she was barren, and We made her bear children; that was her being set right.

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا﴾: the exegetes mentioned that it is the opening of her garment, and through it [Translator's note: the spirit] was breathed into her.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ آيَةً﴾ — (and He did not say "two signs") — because their affair is one. Had "two signs" been said, it would have been correct, because she gave birth while a virgin and Jesus spoke in the cradle; so they would be two signs, since they differ.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾: you put (أمّة واحدة) in the accusative by "cutting off" (al-qaṭʿ) [Translator's note: the Kufan term for the ḥāl]. Al-Ḥasan put it in the nominative, (أمتكم أمةٌ واحدةٌ), making al-umma a khabar (predicate), then going back to "one community" with the nominative, also intending it as a khabar, like His saying: ﴿كَلاَّ إنَّهَا لَظَى نَزَّاعَةٌ لِلشَّوَى﴾.
In the reading of Ubayy, as far as I know: (إنَّها لإَحْدَى الكُبَر نَذِيرٌ للبَشَرِ}, the nominative by repetition (takrīr); and similar to it: (ذُو العَرْشِ المَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ).

farraa:95-95.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَآ﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās read it [Translator's note: the reading attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās appears to have dropped out of the text here; elsewhere it is reported as «وحِرْمٌ»]. More than one person narrated that to me, among them Hushaym from Dāwūd from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Sufyān from ʿUmayr and from Ibn ʿAbbās. ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated to me from his father from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: (وَحِرْمٌ). One of them narrated to me from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī: (وحِرْمٌ عَلَى). The people of Medina and al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: read] (وحَرامٌ) with alif. Ḥarām is more widespread in recitation. It is on a par with your saying ḥill and ḥalāl, ḥirm and ḥarām.

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ﴾: al-ḥadab is every hillock (and raised place).

farraa:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "until, when it is opened, [Translator's note: the true promise] draws near." The entry of the wāw into the apodosis after (حَتّى إذا) is on a par with His saying ﴿حَتَّي إذا جَاءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبوابُها﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهم جَعَل السَّقَايَةَ) [Translator's note: the source quotes it without the wāw; the point is that ʿAbd Allāh's reading has «وجعل»], while in our reading it is without wāw. Similar to it in al-Ṣāffāt: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبينِ وَنَادَيْنَاهُ﴾, its meaning being "We called him". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فلمَّا أَجَزْنا سَاحَةَ الحىّ وانتحى * بنَا بَطْنُ خَبْتٍ ذِى قِفَاف عَقْنَقِل
(When we had crossed the open ground of the tribe, and the hollow of a plain with hillocks and winding sand-dunes drew us aside…)
He means "intaḥā" (without the wāw).
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾: (هى) may be a prop (ʿimād) [Translator's note: the Kufan term for the pronoun of the matter], in whose place (هو) would also be suitable; it would then be like His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ أَنَا اللهُ العَزِيزُ الحكِيمُ﴾. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿فَإنَّها لاَ تَعْمَى الأَبْصَارُ﴾: the feminine came because al-abṣār is feminine, while the masculine would be for the ʿimād. I heard one of the Arabs say: "kāna marratan wa-huwa yanfaʿu al-nāsa aḥsābuhum" ("once upon a time it was the case that people's noble lineages benefited them"), making (هو) an ʿimād. And one of them recited to me:
بثوب ودينارٍ وشاة ودرهمٍ * فَهَل هُوَ مرفوع بما هَا هنا راسُ
(With a garment, a dinar, a ewe and a dirham — is it the case that a head is raised by what is here?)
If you wish, you make (هى) refer to al-abṣār: you referred to them by a pronoun, then made al-abṣār overt to explain it, as the poet said:
لعمرُ أبيها لا تقول ظَعينتى * ألاَ فَرّعنى مالكُ بن أبى كعب
(By the life of her father, my lady in the litter will not say: "Ah, Mālik ibn Abī Kaʿb has abandoned me to fear!")
He mentioned al-ẓaʿīna when he had already referred to her by a pronoun in (laʿamru).

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: it is related that al-ḥaṣab in the dialect of the people of Yemen is firewood (al-ḥaṭab). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥakam al-Kāhilī from a man who heard ʿAlī read (حَطَب) with ṭāʾ. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Madanī narrated to me from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, tracing it back to ʿĀʾisha, that she read (حَطَبُ) likewise. And with a chain of Ibn Abī Yaḥyā from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read (حَضَب) with ḍād. Everything with which you stir up a fire or kindle it is ḥaḍab. As for al-ḥaṣab, it is, in the sense of the dialect of Najd, what you throw into the fire, as in your saying "ḥaṣabtu the man", i.e. I pelted him.

farraa:104-104.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي ٱلسَّمَآءَ﴾: with nūn, and with tāʾ (تُطْوَى). Had it been said (يَطْوِى), as it was said (نطوى) with nūn, it would have been permissible.
The readers agreed on (السّجِلّ) with the doubled consonant.
Most of them say (للكِتَابِ), and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh (للكُتُب). Al-sijill is the scroll. The speech breaks off at "the books"; then it begins anew and says ﴿كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُّعِيدُهُ﴾: the kāf belongs to the creation, as though you said: "We will bring back the creation as We began them (the first time)."
His saying ﴿وَعْداً عَلَيْنَآ﴾ is like your saying "a duty upon Us" (ḥaqqan ʿalaynā).

farraa:105-105.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّ ٱلأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِيَ ٱلصَّالِحُونَ﴾: it is said: the land of Paradise. And it is said: it is the land that the Children of Israel were promised, like His saying: ﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَا القَوْمَ الذِينَ كَانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفونَ مشَارِقَ الأرْضَ وَمغارِبَها﴾.

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي هَـٰذَا لَبَلاَغاً﴾: that is, in the Qurʾān.

farraa:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ﴾: the normal way of the speech is (anna with fatḥa), because (يُوحَى) falls upon it; and (إنَّما) with kasra is permissible. That is because it is a particle, as I described to you from the poet's saying:
* ... أَنْ إنَّما بَيْنَ بِيشَةٍ *
(…that between Bīsha…)
So you drop (أنْ), as though it were said: "It is only revealed to me that indeed your god is one god."

farraa:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿إِنْ أَدْرِي﴾ is nominative [Translator's note: i.e. indicative], in the sense of "I do not know".

farraa:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱحْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ is jussive [Translator's note: i.e. imperative]: a request he made of his Lord. It has also been said: (قل رَبّى أحْكَمُ بالحق), with (أحكم) in the nominative and its alif given a hamza. Whoever says "qul rabbī aḥkamu bi-l-ḥaqq", the position of rabbī is nominative; and whoever says "rabbi -ḥkum" with the joining alif, it is in the position of the accusative as a vocative.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ثم صدقناهم الوعد﴾: ثم: a conjunction; صدقناهم: verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl (object); الوعد: accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition, the original being: صدقناهم في الوعد.
﴿فأنجيناهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction (ʿāṭifa); أنجيناهم: verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl; the clause ﴿أنجيناهم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿صدقناهم﴾.
﴿ومن نشاء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object pronoun in ﴿أنجيناهم﴾; the clause ﴿نشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وأهلكنا المسرفين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أهلكنا: verb and fāʿil; المسرفين: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿أنجيناهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون﴾: لقد: the lām is the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); أنزلنا: verb and fāʿil (agent); إليكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾; كتابًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ذكركم﴾; ذكركم: the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿فيه ذكركم﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتابًا﴾.
﴿أفلا تعقلون﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining to something implied, i.e.: "Do you not reflect, so that you do not understand anything of the things mentioned to you?"; تعقلون: imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وكم قصمنا من قرية كانت ظالمة وأنشأنا بعدها قوما آخرين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; كم is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿قصمنا﴾; من قرية: tamyīz (specification) of the predicative ﴿كم﴾, genitive (majrūr) by مِن; كانت: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ being a particle of the feminine, its noun (ism) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هي; ظالمة: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿كانت ظالمة﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of قرية. The clause ﴿وكم قصمنا...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position. أنشأنا: the wāw is a conjunction, and أنشأنا is verb and fāʿil (agent); بعدها: an adverb of time, accusative with the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنشأنا﴾, and ﴿ها﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); قومًا: mafʿūl bihi; آخرين: a naʿt of ﴿قومًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿فلما أحسوا بأسنا إذا هم منها يركضون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لمّا is temporal (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya, "at the time when") or a linking particle (rābiṭa); أحسوا: past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); بأسنا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إذا is the إذا of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); منها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يركضون﴾; the clause ﴿يركضون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿لا تركضوا وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه ومساكنكم لعلكم تسألون﴾: لا is prohibitive (nāhiya); تركضوا: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿لا تركضوا﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying; ارجعوا: an imperative verb conjoined to ﴿لا تركضوا﴾, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; إلى ما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ارجعوا﴾; the clause ﴿أترفتم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; فيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أترفتم﴾; مساكنكم: in the genitive, conjoined to ما; لعلكم: لعل is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing hope, and ﴿كم﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun (ism) of لعل; تسألون: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw of the plural is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿تسألون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of لعل.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين﴾: يا is a vocative particle; ﴿ويلنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), in a genitive construct (muḍāf), accusative; the clause ﴿يا ويلنا﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of their saying; ﴿إنا﴾: إن is a particle of emphasis and accusative, and ﴿نا﴾ is the noun (ism) of إن; كنا: كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the noun of كان; ظالمين: the khabar (predicate) of كان; the clause ﴿كنا ظالمين﴾ is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿فما زالت تلك دعواهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما زالت: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ being the sign of the feminine; تلك: a demonstrative in the position of nominative as the noun (ism) of ﴿ما زال﴾; دعواهم: its khabar (predicate), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm is a particle indicating the masculine plural.
﴿حتى جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين﴾: حتى: a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; جعلناهم: verb, fāʿil (agent) and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حصيدًا خامدين: second mafʿūl bihi, because their ruling is the ruling of a single word; or حصيدا is the second mafʿūl bihi and خامدين is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حصيدًا﴾ or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in جعلناهم.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; ما: negating; خلقنا: verb and fāʿil (agent); السماء: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض: conjoined to السماء; ما: conjoined to السماء and الأرض; بينهما: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position; لاعبين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of خلقنا; the clause ﴿وما خلقنا السماء...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا لاتخذناه من لدنا إن كنا فاعلين﴾: لو is conditional, of impossibility (imtināʿiyya); أردنا: verb and fāʿil (agent); أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of أردنا; the fāʿil of نتخذ is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن; لهوًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). لاتخذناه: the lām occurs in the answer of لو, and اتخذناه is verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; من لدنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of اتخذ; إن is conditional and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of لو, the implied form being: "If We were doers, We would have taken it — and We are not doers"; or it is negating, meaning ما, i.e.: "We were not doers"; كنا: كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the noun (ism) of كان; فاعلين: the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); نقذف: imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن; بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نقذف﴾; على الباطل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نقذف﴾; and it was said: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "rising above falsehood". فيدمغه: conjoined to نقذف; the fāʾ is a conjunction, يدمغه is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being هو, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). فإذا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); زاهق: its khabar (predicate).
﴿ولكم الويل مما تصفون﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; الويل: the postponed mubtadaʾ; مِن is a preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) or a relative noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the "settledness" (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached; the clause ﴿تصفون﴾ has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وله من في السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); مَن: the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿في السماوات والأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾; the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; مَن is conjoined to the first مَن; عنده: an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of ﴿من﴾, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position; the clause ﴿لا يستكبرون﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the first ﴿من﴾; عن عبادته: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستكبرون﴾; the clause ﴿لا يستحسرون﴾ is conjoined to the clause لا يستكبرون. Or the wāw in ﴿ومن عنده﴾ is resumptive, ومن عنده is a mubtadaʾ, the clause ﴿لا يستكبرون﴾ is its khabar, and the clause ﴿ومن عنده...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; يسبحون: imperfect verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿لا يفترون﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يسبحون.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون﴾: أم: a conjunction, and it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the interrogative hamza, the interrogation being one of disapproval (inkārī); اتخذوا: verb and fāʿil (agent); آلهة: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿ينشرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿هم ينشرون﴾ is a naʿt of آلهة, or resumptive with no grammatical position; the object of ينشرون is omitted, i.e.: "they resurrect the dead".

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا﴾: لو is conditional, of impossibility (imtināʿiyya); كان: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; فيهما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; آلهة: the postponed noun (ism) of كان; إلا means غير ("other than") and is a naʿt (adjective) of آلهة; it cannot validly be an exceptive particle, because the implication of exception is unsound here, since its upshot would be that if there were in them gods from whom Allah was not excepted, they would not be ruined — and that is not so, for the mere multiplicity of gods necessarily entails ruin absolutely. لفسدتا: the lām occurs in the answer of لو, and فسدتا is verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause فسدتا has no grammatical position.
﴿فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; سبحان: standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb; the word of majesty (Allah) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); رب العرش: a badal (substitute) or naʿt of the word of majesty; عما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to سبحان; the clause ﴿يصفون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a genitive maṣdar (verbal noun), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿سبحان﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; لا is negating; يسأل: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو; عما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسأل﴾; the clause ﴿يفعل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. وهم: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿يسألون﴾ is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة﴾: أم: a conjunction, and it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the interrogative hamza, the interrogation being one of disapproval (inkārī); اتخذوا: past verb and fāʿil (agent); من دونه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of اتخذوا; آلهة is the first mafʿūl.
﴿قل هاتوا برهانكم﴾: هاتوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; برهانكم: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي﴾: هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); ذكر: khabar (predicate); مَن: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); معي: an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position; ذكر: conjoined to the first ذكر; مَن: muḍāf ilayhi; قبلي: an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); أكثرهم: mubtadaʾ; the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ is the khabar, the wāw is the fāʿil, and الحق is mafʿūl bihi. فهم: the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīl); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ; معرضون: khabar.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ما is negating; أرسلنا: verb and fāʿil (agent); من قبلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); مِن is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; رسول is genitive in form and accusative in position as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); نوحي: verb and fāʿil; إليه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نوحي﴾; أنه: أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is the noun (ism) of أن; لا is the lā of generic negation, and ﴿إله﴾ is the noun of لا, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative; إلا is a particle of restriction; أنا is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun latent in the khabar (predicate) of لا; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أن, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أنه...﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿نوحي﴾. ﴿فاعبدون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ, implying an omitted condition); اعبدون: an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ, omitted in accordance with the script of the Muṣḥaf, is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; قالوا: verb and fāʿil (agent); اتخذ: past verb; الرحمن: fāʿil; ولدا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿اتخذ الرحمن ولدا﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of the saying, in the position of accusative.
﴿سبحانه﴾: standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); together with its omitted verb it is a parenthetical clause with no grammatical position.
﴿بل عباد مكرمون﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); عباد: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هم; مكرمون: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿لا يسبقونه بالقول﴾: لا is negating; يسبقونه: verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl (object); بالقول: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسبقون﴾; the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عباد﴾, in the position of nominative.
﴿وهم بأمره يعملون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بأمره﴾: preposition, genitive noun and muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يعملون﴾; يعملون: verb and fāʿil; the clause ﴿يعملون﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم﴾: يعلم: imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; ما: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بين: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position; أيديهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative; خلفهم: an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position, and the pronoun ﴿هم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿يعلم ما بين أيديهم﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عباد﴾, in the position of nominative.
﴿ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating; يشفعون: imperfect verb and fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); لمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يشفعون﴾; ارتضى: past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being هو; the clause ﴿ارتضى﴾ is the ṣila of the relative, with no grammatical position. ﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿هم﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿من خشيته﴾: preposition, genitive noun and muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿مشفقون﴾; مشفقون: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; مَن is conditional, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يقل: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ﴿يقل﴾; the clause ﴿يقل﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of مَن. ﴿إني﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun (ism); ﴿إله﴾: the khabar of إن; ﴿من دونه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿إله﴾; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because it is a nominal clause; ذلك: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; نجزيه: imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being نحن; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb نجزي, and جهنم is the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb نجزي; the clause ﴿نجزيه﴾ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿فذلك نجزيه جهنم﴾ is the apodosis of the condition.
﴿كذلك نجزي الظالمين﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: "with a recompense like that do We recompense"; ذلك: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿نجزي﴾: imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: نحن; ﴿الظالمين﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, of conversion (to the past) and of the jussive; ير: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter; الذين: fāʿil (agent); كفروا: verb and fāʿil; the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; أنّ is abrogating (nāsikha); السماوات: the noun (ism) of أن; الأرض: conjoined to السماوات. ﴿كانتا﴾: كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb, the tāʾ is a particle of the feminine, and the alif is the noun of كان; رتقًا: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿كانتا رتقا﴾ is the khabar of أن; أنّ with its noun and its khabar fills the place of the two objects of ﴿يرَ﴾. ﴿ففتقناهما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; فتقناهما: verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿فتقناهما﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿كانتا رتقا﴾.
﴿وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا: verb and fāʿil, meaning "We created"; من الماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعلنا﴾, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿كل شيء﴾, because it was originally a description of it, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl; كل شيء: object; حي: a naʿt (adjective) of شيء. Or ﴿جعلنا﴾ means "We made (something into something)" and so takes two objects, in which case ﴿من الماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second object, and ﴿كل شيء﴾ is the first object.
﴿أفلا يؤمنون﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining to something omitted; لا is negating; يؤمنون: imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا: verb and fāʿil (agent), conjoined to the preceding جعلنا; ﴿في الأرض﴾ is either a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object, with ﴿رواسي﴾ being the first object, or a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جعلنا﴾ or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from رواسي, with ﴿رواسي﴾ being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أن and what lies within its scope are in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿بهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تميد﴾.
﴿وجعلنا فيها فجاجا سبلا لعلهم يهتدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا: verb and fāʿil, conjoined to the preceding جعلنا; ﴿فيها﴾ is either a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second object, with سبلا being the first object, or a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جعلنا﴾, with سبلا the mafʿūl bihi; فجاجًا: a ḥāl, because it was a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سبلا﴾ and was placed before it; سبلا: mafʿūl bihi; لعلهم: لعل is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism); يهتدون: verb and fāʿil; the clause ﴿يهتدون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of لعل.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا: verb and fāʿil (agent), conjoined to the preceding جعلنا; السماء: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); سقفًا: second mafʿūl bihi; محفوظا: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سقفا﴾.
﴿وهم عن آياتها معرضون﴾: the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); عن آياتها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿معرضون﴾; معرضون: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾; the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿خلق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position; the fāʿil (agent) of خلق is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; الليل: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and what follows it is conjoined to it.
﴿كل في فلك يسبحون﴾: كل: mubtadaʾ; في فلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسبحون﴾; the clause ﴿يسبحون﴾ is the khabar of كل; the clause ﴿كل في فلك يسبحون﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ما is negating; جعلنا: verb and fāʿil (agent); لبشر: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object; من قبلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of بشر; الخلد: the first object of جعلنا.
﴿أفإن مت فهم الخالدون﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; ﴿مِتَّ﴾: past verb and fāʿil, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); الخالدون: khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿كل نفس ذائقة الموت﴾: كل: mubtadaʾ (subject); نفس: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿ذائقة﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿الموت﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; نبلوكم: imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالشر: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نبلوكم﴾; الخير: conjoined to الشر; فتنة: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a synonym of the maṣdar (verbal noun).
﴿وإلينا ترجعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إلينا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ترجعون﴾; ترجعون: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿نبلوكم﴾; and it was said: circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; إذا: an adverb for future time; رآك: past verb, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين: the fāʿil (agent) of رآك; كفروا: verb and fāʿil; the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿رآك﴾ is in the position of genitive through the adverb's being annexed to it; إن is negating; يتخذونك: imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the negating إن and what lies within its scope are the answer of إذا; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); هزوًا: second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿يذكر﴾ is the ṣila of الذي, with no grammatical position; the fāʿil of يذكر is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو; آلهتكم: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿أهذا الذي ...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the speech (maqūl) of an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "they take you in mockery, saying: ﴿أهذا الذي ...﴾".
﴿وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ; بذكر: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كافرون﴾; الرحمن: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the second ﴿هم﴾ is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the first ﴿هم﴾. The clause ﴿وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون﴾ is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يتخذونك.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿خلق الإنسان من عجل﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; خلق: a past verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named); الإنسان: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); من عجل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلق﴾ or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون﴾: the sīn is for the future; ﴿أريكم﴾: imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنا, and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). آياتي: second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive (nāhiya); تستعجلون: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ, omitted for the script, is mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿سأريكم﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; يقولون: imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); متى: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); هذا: the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); الوعد: badal (substitute); إن is conditional; ﴿كنتم﴾: كان is a past verb, and ﴿تم﴾ is its noun (ism); ﴿صادقين﴾: the khabar of كنتم; ﴿كنتم﴾ is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis (jawāb) of إن is omitted, its implied form being: "then specify its appointed time".

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار﴾: لو is conditional; يعلم: imperfect verb; الذين: fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; حين: an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted object of يعلم; the clause ﴿لا يكفون﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of genitive; عن وجوههم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفون﴾; ﴿النار﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولا عن ظهورهم﴾: conjoined.
﴿ولا هم ينصرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating; ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ينصرون: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿ينصرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿هم﴾; the answer of لو is omitted, its implied form being: "they would not have sought to hasten the punishment".

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿بل تأتيهم بغتة﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; تأتيهم: imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and mafʿūl (object); ﴿بغتة﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿فتبهتهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تبهتهم: imperfect verb, latent fāʿil and mafʿūl; the clause ﴿تبهتهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تأتيهم﴾.
﴿فلا يستطيعون ردها﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is negating; يستطيعون: imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; ﴿رَدَّها﴾: the object of يستطيعون.
﴿ولا هم ينظرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating; ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ينظرون: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw of the plural is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿ينظرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); استهزئ: a past verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named); ﴿برسل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿من قبلك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رسل.
﴿فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; حاق: past verb; بالذين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿حاق﴾; the clause ﴿سخروا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سخروا﴾, or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of سخروا. ﴿ما﴾: the fāʿil of حاق; كانوا: كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the noun (ism) of كان; ﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to His saying يستهزئون; يستهزئون is a verbal clause in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن﴾: مَن is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿يكلؤكم﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿من يكلؤكم ...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the speech (maqūl) of the saying; بالليل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكلؤكم﴾; النهار: conjoined to الليل; من الرحمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكلؤكم﴾.
﴿بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ; عن ذكر ربهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿معرضون﴾; ﴿معرضون﴾: the khabar of ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا﴾: أم is a particle of conjunction and of digression (iḍrāb), meaning بل plus the hamza, i.e.: "Nay, do they have gods?"; ﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); آلهة: the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿تمنعهم﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of آلهة; ﴿من دوننا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of ﴿آلهة﴾ as well.
﴿لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; لا is negating; يستطيعون: imperfect verb and fāʿil (agent); نصر: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أنفسهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negating; ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ; منا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يصحبون﴾; يصحبون: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿يصحبون﴾ is the khabar of ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); متعنا: verb and fāʿil (agent); هؤلاء: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); آباءهم: conjoined to هؤلاء; حتى: a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; طال: past verb; ﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿طال﴾; العمر: the fāʿil of طال.
﴿أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining to something implied; لا is negating; يرون: imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; أنّ and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of يرون, because the "seeing" here is of knowledge (ʿilmiyya); it may also be visual (baṣariyya), in which case the verb ﴿يرون﴾ takes a single object. ﴿أنّا﴾: أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun (ism); the clause ﴿نأتي الأرض﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of أن; the clause ﴿ننقصها من أطرافها﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the fāʿil of نأتي or from its object.
﴿أفهم الغالبون﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining to something implied; ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); الغالبون: khabar.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي﴾: إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) particle; أنذركم: imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنا, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالوحي: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنذركم﴾.
﴿ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لا is negating; يسمع: imperfect verb; الصم: fāʿil; الدعاء: mafʿūl bihi; إذا is an adverb for future time, here purely adverbial, attached to ﴿يسمع﴾, i.e.: "at the time of their being warned"; ما is redundant (ṣila); ينذرون: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿ينذرون﴾ is in the position of genitive through the adverb's being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; مستهم: a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); نفحة: fāʿil (agent); ﴿من عذاب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نفحة﴾. ﴿ليقولن﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of the oath, because it came first; يقولن: imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis. ﴿يا ويلنا﴾: ﴿يا﴾ is a vocative particle, and ﴿ويلنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), in a genitive construct (muḍāf), accusative; the clause ﴿يا ويلنا﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of their saying; ﴿إنا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun (ism); ﴿كنا﴾: كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ظالمين: the khabar (predicate) of كان; the clause ﴿كنا ظالمين﴾ is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; نضع: imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being نحن; الموازين: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); القسط: a naʿt (adjective) of الموازين, described by the maṣdar (verbal noun) for intensiveness; ﴿ليوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نضع﴾, and القيامة is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فلا تظلم نفس شيئا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تظلم: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named); نفس: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); شيئًا: second object of تظلم, or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being a description of the maṣdar.
﴿وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كان: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its noun (ism) is latent, its implied form being هو, referring to the deed; ﴿مثقال حبة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of كان; ﴿من خردل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of حبة; ﴿أتينا بها﴾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿وكفى بنا حاسبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; كفى: past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; ﴿حاسبين﴾: tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); آتينا: verb and fāʿil (agent); ﴿موسى﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿هارون﴾: conjoined to موسى; الفرقان: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿ولقد آتينا موسى...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position; ضياء: conjoined to الفرقان, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it with the wāw redundant (ṣila); ذكرًا: conjoined to ضياء; للمتقين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ذكرا﴾ or to a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ذكرا﴾.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t:
﴿الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب﴾: الذين: a relative noun in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المتقين, or in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being ﴿هم﴾; the clause ﴿يخشون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ربهم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بالغيب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil in يخشون.
﴿وهم من الساعة مشفقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾: mubtadaʾ; من الساعة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مشفقون﴾; مشفقون: the khabar of ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه﴾: the wāw is resumptive; هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); ذكر: khabar (predicate); مبارك: a naʿt (adjective); أنزلناه: verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿وهذا ذكر مبارك﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿أنزلناه﴾ is a naʿt of ذكر.
﴿أفأنتم له منكرون﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining to something omitted; أنتم: mubtadaʾ; ﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿منكرون﴾; منكرون: the khabar of أنتم.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); آتينا: verb and fāʿil (agent); إبراهيم: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); رشده: second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿من قبل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); كنا: the wāw is a conjunction, and كان is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) [Translator's note: كان is a verb (one of kāna and its sisters); the source calls it a ḥarf here], and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun (ism); ﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عالمين; عالمين: the khabar (predicate) of كنا; the clause ﴿كنا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آتينا﴾.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾: an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿آتينا﴾ or ﴿رشده﴾ or ﴿عالمين﴾ in the preceding ayah; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); لأبيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قال﴾; قومه: conjoined to ﴿لأبيه﴾; ما: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); هذه: khabar (predicate); التماثيل: a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; التي: a naʿt (adjective); the clause ﴿أنتم لها عاكفون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, with no grammatical position; أنتم: mubtadaʾ; عاكفون: khabar; ﴿لها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عاكفون﴾; the clause ﴿ما هذه ...﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of the saying, in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿قالوا وجدنا آباءنا لها عابدين﴾: قالوا: verb and fāʿil (agent); وجدنا: verb and fāʿil; آباءنا: the first object of وجدنا; ﴿لها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عابدين; عابدين: the second object of وجدنا; the clause ﴿وجدنا﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of the saying, in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿قال لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين﴾: the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); كنتم: كان, and the tāʾ is its noun (ism); أنتم: tawkīd (emphasis) of the tāʾ; آباؤكم: conjoined to the tāʾ; ﴿في ضلال﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of كنتم; مبين: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ضلال﴾.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿قالوا أجئتنا بالحق أم أنت من اللاعبين﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; جئتنا: verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جئتنا﴾; أم: a conjunction that is the counterpart (muʿādil) of the hamza; أنت: mubtadaʾ (subject); من اللاعبين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause ﴿أجئتنا ...﴾ is the speech (maqūl) of the saying, in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿قال بل ربكم رب السماوات والأرض الذي فطرهن﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿ربكم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); رب السماوات والأرض: khabar (predicate); الذي: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رب﴾; ﴿فطرهن﴾: past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿فطرهن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position.
﴿وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين﴾: أنا: mubtadaʾ; ﴿من الشاهدين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿على ذلكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to الشاهدين.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿وتالله لأكيدن أصنامكم بعد أن تولوا مدبرين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the oath; the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿تالله﴾ are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: "I swear"; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; أكيدن: imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is emphasised with the heavy nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنا; أصنامكم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بعد: an adverb attached to ﴿أكيدن﴾; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن﴾ and what lies within its scope is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); مدبرين: ḥāl (circumstantial).
