zajjaj:8-8.t: And His words: ﴿وَما جَعَلْناهم جَسَدًا لا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ﴾ — ”جَسَدًا“ is a singular that conveys a group, i.e. ”وَما جَعَلْناهم ذَوِي أجْسادٍ، إلّا لِيَأْكُلُوا الطَّعامَ“ ("We did not make them possessors of bodies except that they should eat food"). That is because they had said: ﴿مالِ هَذا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ﴾ [al-Furqān: 7], so they were informed that all the messengers eat food and that they die; and that is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَما كانُوا خالِدِينَ﴾.

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His words: ﴿لَقَدْ أنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكم كِتابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ﴾, i.e. in it is a reminder for you of the mercy or punishment you will meet, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَلا إنَّها تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 11]. It has also been said: ”فِيهِ ذِكُرُكُمْ“: in it is your honour.

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His words: ﴿وَكَمْ قَصَمْنا مِن قَرْيَةٍ كانَتْ ظالِمَةً﴾ — ”كَمْ“ is in the position of the accusative, governed by ”قَصَمْنا“. The meaning of ”قَصَمْنا“ is: We destroyed and did away with. One says ”قَصَمَ اللَّهُ عُمْرَ الكافِرِ“ ("Allah cut off the life of the disbeliever"), i.e. He did away with it.

zajjaj:12-12.t: And His words: ﴿فَلَمّا أحَسُّوا بَأْسَنا إذا هم مِنها يَرْكُضُونَ﴾, i.e. they flee from the punishment.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿لا تَرْكُضُوا وارْجِعُوا إلى ما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ ومَساكِنِكم لَعَلَّكم تُسْألُونَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that this was said to them by way of mockery. It was also said: ”لَعَلَّكم تُسْألُونَ شَيْئًا مِمّا أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ“ ("perhaps you will be asked for something of the luxury you enjoyed"). It may also mean: ”لَعَلَّكم تُسْألُونَ فَتُجِيبُونَ عَمّا تُشاهِدُونَ إذا رَأيْتُمْ ما نَزَلَ بِمَساكِنِكُمْ، وما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ“ ("perhaps you will be asked and will answer about what you witness when you see what has befallen your dwellings and the luxury you enjoyed").

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His words: ﴿قالُوا يا ويْلَنا إنّا كُنّا ظالِمِينَ﴾ — ”وَيْلٌ“ is a word said of everyone who has fallen into ruin, and likewise everyone who falls into ruin says it.

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His words: ﴿فَما زالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْواهُمْ﴾, i.e. the word that is their saying ”يا ويْلَنا إنّا كُنّا ظالِمِينَ“ did not cease to be their cry. ”تِلْكَ“ may be in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of ”زالَتْ“, and ”دَعْواهُمْ“ in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ”زالَتْ“; and it is possible that ”دَعْواهُمْ“ is the noun, in the position of the nominative, and ”تِلْكَ“ in the position of the accusative as the khabar. There is no disagreement among the grammarians about the two possibilities.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
And His words: ﴿لَوْ أرَدْنا أنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لاتَّخَذْناهُ مِن لَدُنّا إنْ كُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾ — ”اَللَّهْوُ“ in the dialect of Ḥaḍramawt is "the child". It was also said: ”اَللَّهْوُ“ is the woman [wife]. Its interpretation is that the child is the diversion of this world; so: if We had wanted to take something of diversion with which one is diverted. The meaning of ﴿لاتَّخَذْناهُ مِن لَدُنّا﴾ is: We would have chosen it from what We create.
﴿إنْ كُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾ — its meaning is: ”ما كُنّا فاعِلِينَ“ ("We were not going to do [so]"), and so it has come in the exegesis. It may also be conditional, i.e. ”إنْ كُنّا مِمَّنْ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ، ولَسْنا مِمَّنْ يَفْعَلُهُ“ ("if We were among those who do that — and We are not among those who do it"). The first view is the view of the exegetes and the second is the view of the grammarians, yet all of them state the first view and consider it good, because ”إنْ“ can be in the sense of negation; except that most often it comes with the lām: you say ”إنْ كُنْتَ لَصالِحًا“, meaning ”ما كُنْتَ إلّا صالِحًا“ ("you were nothing but righteous").

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His words: ﴿بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالحَقِّ عَلى الباطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ﴾ — by "the truth" is meant ”اَلْقُرْآنُ“ (the Qurʾān), [hurled] against their falsehood. ”فَيَدْمَغُهُ“: so it makes it vanish in abasement and humiliation. ﴿فَإذا هو زاهِقٌ﴾, i.e. vanishing. ﴿وَلَكُمُ الوَيْلُ مِمّا تَصِفُونَ﴾, i.e. for the lies you tell in your description, in your saying that Allah has a child.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His words: ﴿وَلَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ ومَن عِنْدَهُ﴾, i.e. these whom you have claimed to be the children of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, are the servants of Allah, and they are the angels.
And His words: ﴿لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ ولا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ﴾, i.e. they do not grow weary. One says ”حَسِرَ، واسْتَحْسَرَ“ when one tires and becomes exhausted; so the angels do not grow weary.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ والنَّهارَ لا يَفْتُرُونَ﴾, i.e. no mission distracts them from glorification; glorification runs in them as breathing runs in us — nothing distracts us from breathing, and likewise their glorification is constant.

zajjaj:21-21.t: And His words: ﴿أمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الأرْضِ هم يُنْشِرُونَ﴾ — also ”يَنْشُرُونَ“. Whoever reads ”يُنْشِرُونَ“, its meaning is: ”أمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً يُحْيُونَ المَوْتى“ ("or have they taken gods who bring the dead to life?"); one says ”أنْشَرَ اللَّهُ المَوْتى“ ("Allah raised the dead") and ”نُشِرُوا هُمْ“ ("they were raised"). Whoever reads ”يَنْشُرُونَ“ with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, its meaning is: ”أمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً لا يَمُوتُونَ، يَحْيَوْنَ أبَدًا“ ("or have they taken gods who do not die, who live forever?").

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His words: ﴿لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إلا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا﴾ — ”فِيهِما“: in the heaven and the earth. ”إلّا“ is in the sense of ”غَيْرُ“ ("other than"); the meaning is: ”لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ لَفَسَدَتا“ ("had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined"). So ”إلّا“ is an attribute (ṣifa) in the sense of ”غَيْرُ“, and for that reason what follows it is nominative, following the form of what precedes it. The poet said:
؎وَكُلُّ أخٍ مُفارِقُهُ أخُوهُ لَعَمْرُ أبِيكَ إلّا الفَرْقَدانِ
(Every brother will be parted from by his brother — by your father's life! — other than the two Farqad stars.)
The meaning is: ”وَكُلُّ أخٍ غَيْرُ الفَرْقَدَيْنِ مُفارِقُهُ أخُوهُ“ ("every brother other than the two Farqads will be parted from by his brother").
And His words: ﴿فَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ العَرْشِ عَمّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ — ”سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ“ means: declaring Allah free of all evil. We have explained that already, and this is an explanation from the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:23-23.t: And His words: ﴿لا يُسْألُ عَمّا يَفْعَلُ وهم يُسْألُونَ﴾, i.e. He is not asked at the Resurrection about His judgement concerning His servants, while He asks His servants about their deeds — the questioning of one who rebukes, for whoever deserves rebuke, and requiting with forgiveness whoever deserves that. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, already knows the deeds of the servants, but He asks them in order to establish the proof against them; and that is His saying: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24], i.e. the questioning of proof that we have mentioned. As for His saying: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 39], its meaning is: ”لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ لِيُسْتَعْلَمَ مِنهُ“ ("he will not be asked about his sin in order that it be learned from him"), because Allah knew their deeds before they took place, when they took place and after they took place — ”عالِمُ الغَيْبِ والشَّهادَةِ“ ("Knower of the unseen and the witnessed").

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ هاتُوا بُرْهانَكم هَذا ذِكْرُ مَن مَعِيَ وذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِي﴾ — Allah had made the proof against them clear in establishing His oneness and that their gods avail them nothing. Then it was said to them: Bring your proof that any one of the messengers informed his community that they had a god other than Allah! Is there in the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me anything but the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?!
It has also been read: ”هَذا ذِكْرٌ مِن مَعِي وذِكْرٌ مِن قَبْلِي“, and its justification is good. Its meaning is: ”هَذا ذِكْرٌ مِمّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيَّ، مِمّا هو مَعِي، وذِكْرٌ مِن قَبْلِي“ ("this is a reminder from what has been sent down to me, from what is with me, and a reminder from before me"). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: by His saying ”مَن مَعِيَ“ he means ”مِنَ الَّذِي عِنْدِي“ ("from what I have") or ”مِنَ الَّذِي قَبْلِي“ ("from what was before me").
Then He made it clear, saying: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَسُولٍ إلا نُوحِي إلَيْهِ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 25] — also ”يُوحى إلَيْهِ“, and ”يُوحِي إلَيْهِ“ is permissible — ﴿أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا أنا فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 25].

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His words: ﴿وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ ولَدًا سُبْحانَهُ بَلْ عِبادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ — meant are the angels and ʿĪsā son of Maryam, peace be upon him; what is in the exegesis is that they are the angels. If it were read ”بَلْ عِبادًا مُكْرَمِينَ“, that would not be permissible, as it contradicts the muṣḥaf, though in Arabic it is permissible, the meaning being: ”بَلِ اتَّخَذَ عِبادًا مُكْرَمِينَ“ ("rather He has taken honoured servants"). The nominative is better and finer.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His words: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنَّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ كانَتا رَتْقًا﴾ — He said ”كانَتا“ (dual) because the heavens are referred to with a singular word, and the heavens were a single heaven, and likewise the earths were a single earth. So the meaning is that the heavens were a single heaven, closed up, with no water in it; then Allah split the heaven open and made it seven, and made the earth seven earths. It has come in the exegesis that the heaven was split open with rain and the earth with vegetation; and what indicates that by its splitting is meant the coming of rain from it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِنَ الماءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾.
He said ”رَتْقًا“ and did not say ”رَتْقَيْنِ“ (dual) because ”اَلرَّتْقُ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is: ”كانَتا ذَواتَيْ رَتْقٍ“ ("the two were possessed of closure"), and then they were made possessed of splitting. By this He guided them to His oneness, Majestic and Mighty is He; then He rebuked them, saying: ﴿أفَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
And His words: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا في الأرْضِ رَواسِيَ أنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ﴾ — the meaning is: ”كَراهَةَ أنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ“ ("out of aversion to its swaying with them"). Some said its meaning is: ”ألّا تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ“ ("so that it would not sway with them"), and the meaning is indeed so, except that ”لا“ is not implied, whereas the muḍāf (annexed noun) can be omitted; and ”كَراهَةَ أنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ“ conveys the meaning of ”ألّا تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ“. The meaning of ”تَمِيدُ“ in the language is "it spins"; one who becomes dizzy when he travels by sea is called ”مائِدٌ“ and [plural] ”مَيْدى“. ”اَلرَّواسِي“ means ”اَلْجِبالُ الثَّوابِتُ“ ("the firm mountains").
﴿وَجَعَلْنا فِيها فِجاجًا سُبُلا﴾ — ”فِجاجٌ“ is the plural of ”فَجٌّ“, which is any gap between two mountains, and ”سُبُلًا“ means roads.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿وَجَعَلْنا السَّماءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ — Allah protected it from falling on the earth except by His leave. It was also said: "protected", i.e. protected by the stars, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنّا زَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِزِينَةٍ الكَواكِبِ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 6] ﴿وَحِفْظًا مِن كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ مارِدٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 7].
﴿وَهم عَنْ آياتِها مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: and they turn away from its sun, its moon and its stars. It has also been read ”عَنْ آيَتِها“ (singular), and its interpretation is that the sign in it, in itself, is the greatest sign, because it is held up by His power, Mighty and Majestic is He. Something that comprises many signs may be called ”آيَةٌ“ (a sign), meaning that it, as a whole, is evidence of the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
And His words: ﴿كُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ — ”يَسْبَحُونَ“ was said [with the plural of rational beings] as is said of what has reason, because these things were described with action as one who has reason is described. Similarly the Arabs said — in the report of all the grammarians — ”أكَلُونِي البَراغِيثُ“ ("the fleas ate me", with a plural verb): when they were described as eating, ”أكَلُونِي“ was said. The poet said:
؎شَرِبَتْ بِها والدِّيكُ يَدْعُو صَباحَهُ إذا ما بَنُو نَعْشٍ دَنَوْا فَتَصَوَّبُوا
(I drank there while the cock was calling its morning, when the Daughters of the Bier drew near and dipped low.)

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَإنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ — it is read ”مُتَّ“ with a ḍamma on the mīm and ”مِتَّ“ with a kasra; most of the readers have the ḍamma. We have already explained what is in this chapter. The fāʾ entered on ”إنْ“ as the response to the condition, just as it enters in your saying ”إنْ زُرْتَنِي فَأنا أخُوكَ“ ("if you visit me, then I am your brother"); and the fāʾ entered on ”هُمْ“ because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of ”إنْ“. [Translator's note: the text says the fāʾ "entered on «إنْ»"; it is translated as written — the interrogative hamza is followed by the fāʾ, which itself prefixes «إنْ».]

zajjaj:36-36.t:
And His words: ﴿أهَذا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ — this is on the basis of an implied report of speech; the meaning is: ”وَإذا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إلّا هُزُوًا يَقُولُونَ: أهَذا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ؟!“ ("when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery, saying: is this the one who mentions your gods?!"). The meaning is: ”أهَذا الَّذِي يَعِيبُ آلِهَتَكُمْ؟!“ ("is this the one who disparages your gods?!"). One says ”فُلانٌ يَذْكُرُ النّاسَ“, i.e. he backbites them and mentions their faults; and one says ”فُلانٌ يَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ“, i.e. he describes Him with greatness, praises Him and affirms His oneness. With "mentioning" (dhikr), only that whose meaning is understood is omitted. The poet said:
؎لا تَذْكُرِي فَرَسِي وما أطْعَمْتُهُ فَيَكُونَ لَوْنُكِ مِثْلَ لَوْنِ الأجْرَبِ
(Do not mention my horse and what I have fed him, lest your colour become like the colour of the mangy one.)
The meaning is: ”لا تَذْكُرِي فَرَسِي وإحْسانِي إلَيْهِ فَتَعِيبِينِي بِإيثارِي إيّاهُ عَلَيْكِ“ ("do not mention my horse and my kindness to him, reproaching me for preferring him over you").

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُلِقَ الإنْسانُ مِن عَجَلٍ﴾ — the lexicographers said: the meaning is ”خُلِقَتِ العَجَلَةُ مِنَ الإنْسانِ“ ("haste was created from [i.e. in] man"), and its true sense is indicated by: ﴿وَكانَ الإنْسانُ عَجُولا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 11]. The Arabs were addressed only with what they understand, and the Arabs say to one who does something a great deal: ”خُلِقْتَ مِنهُ“ ("you were created from it"), just as they say ”أنْتَ مِن لَعِبٍ“ ("you are of play") and ”خُلِقْتَ مِن لَعِبٍ“ ("you were created from play"), meaning to describe him emphatically with playfulness.

zajjaj:39-39.t: And His words: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النّارَ﴾, i.e. when they cannot push the Fire away from their faces. The apodosis (jawāb) of ”لَوْ“ is omitted; the meaning is: ”لَعَلِمُوا صِدْقَ الوَعْدِ“ ("they would have known the truth of the promise"), because they had said: When is this promise, if you are truthful? And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made the Hour their appointed time.

zajjaj:40-40.t: Then He said: ﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ — ”بَغْتَةً“: suddenly, while they are heedless of it; ”فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ“: and it bewilders them.

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكم بِاللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — its meaning, and Allah knows best, is: ”مَن يَحْفَظُكم مِن بَأْسِ الرَّحْمَنِ؟“ ("who will protect you from the might of the Most Merciful?"), as He said: ﴿فَمَن يَنْصُرُنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ [Hūd: 63], i.e. from the punishment of Allah.

zajjaj:44-44.t: And His words: ﴿أفَهُمُ الغالِبُونَ﴾, i.e. it has become clear to you that We diminish the land from its borders, and that victory is Ours. We have explained ”نَأْتِي الأرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِن أطْرافِها“ in Sūrat al-Raʿd. I.e. ”فاللَّهُ الغالِبُ، وهُمُ المَغْلُوبُونَ“ ("Allah is the victor and they are the vanquished") — I mean the party of Satan.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His words: ﴿وَلا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعاءَ إذا ما يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ — ”وَلا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ“ ("and you do not make the deaf hear the call") is also permissible. ”اَلصُّمُّ“ ("the deaf") here are those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah that is recited to them, so they are like one who does not hear, as the poet said:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to what displeases him, [though] hearing.)

zajjaj:46-46.t: And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهم نَفْحَةٌ مِن عَذابِ رَبِّكَ﴾, i.e. if the least thing of the punishment touches them, ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ يا ويْلَنا إنّا كُنّا ظالِمِينَ﴾. ”اَلْوَيْلُ“ ("woe") is something called out, and everyone who falls into ruin calls it out.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَضَعُ المَوازِينَ القِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ — ”اَلْقِسْطَ“ is justice; the meaning is: ”وَنَضَعُ المَوازِينَ ذَواتِ القِسْطِ“ ("We shall set up the scales possessing justice"). ”قِسْطٌ“, like ”عَدْلٌ“, is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description: you say ”مِيزانٌ قِسْطٌ“ ("a just scale"), ”مِيزانانِ قِسْطٌ“ ("two just scales") and ”مَوازِينُ قِسْطٌ“ ("just scales"). As for ”اَلْمِيزانُ“ at the Resurrection, it has come in the exegesis that it has a tongue and two pans, and deeds are represented by what is weighed. It has come in the exegesis that the conclusion of one's deeds is what is weighed: whoever's final deed is good is rewarded with good, and whoever's final deed is evil, his recompense is evil.
And His words: ﴿وَإنْ كانَ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ﴾ — ”مِثْقالَ“ is accusative in the sense of ”وَإنْ كانَ العَمَلُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ“ ("even if the deed is the weight of a mustard seed"). It is also read ”وَإنْ كانَ مِثْقالُ حَبَّةٍ“ with the nominative, in the sense of ”وَإنْ حَصَلَ لِلْعَبْدِ مِثْقالُ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ أتَيْنا بِها“ ("if the servant has the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it"). ”أتَيْنا بِها“ means "We will bring it"; it has also been read ”آتَيْنا بِها“, in the sense of "We will requite it and give for it". ”أتَيْنا بِها“ is finer as a reading and nearer to the hope of pardon.
﴿وَكَفى بِنا حاسِبِينَ﴾ — [”حاسِبِينَ“] is accusative in two ways: as a tamyīz (specification) and as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The bāʾ entered in ”وَكَفى بِنا“ because it is a statement in the sense of a command; the meaning is: ”اِكْتَفُوا بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا“ ("be content with Allah as Reckoner").

zajjaj:48-48.t: And His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى وهارُونَ الفُرْقانَ وضِياءً وذِكْرًا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ — it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he held that the wāw should be dropped. Some of the grammarians said its meaning is: ”وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى وهارُونَ الفَرْقانِ ضِياءً“ ("We gave Mūsā and Hārūn the Criterion as an illumination"). [Translator's note: ”الفَرْقانِ“ is vowelled thus in the text.] According to the Basrans, the wāw is not added as redundant (zāʾida) and comes only with the sense of conjunction. The interpretation of ”اَلْفُرْقانَ“ is the Torah, in which is the distinction between the lawful and the unlawful. ”ضِياءً“ here is like His saying: ﴿فِيهِ هُدًى ونُورٌ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 46]. ”وَذِكْرى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ“ is also permissible.

zajjaj:50-50.t: And His words: ﴿وَهَذا ذِكْرٌ مُبارَكٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ﴾ — the meaning is: ”هَذا القُرْآنُ ذِكْرٌ مُبارَكٌ“ ("this Qurʾān is a blessed reminder").

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا إبْراهِيمَ رُشْدَهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, i.e. We gave him his guidance as a youth; and it is like His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنا لآتَيْنا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُداها﴾ [al-Sajda: 13].

zajjaj:52-52.t: And His words: ﴿إذْ قالَ لأبِيهِ وقَوْمِهِ ما هَذِهِ التَّماثِيلُ الَّتِي أنْتُمْ لَها عاكِفُونَ﴾ — ”إذْ“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: ”آتَيْناهُ رُشْدَهُ في ذَلِكَ الوَقْتِ“ ("We gave him his guidance at that time"). The meaning of ”اَلتَّماثِيلُ“ here is the idols, and the meaning of ʿukūf is staying devotedly at something.

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His words: ﴿وَتاللَّهِ لأكِيدَنَّ أصْنامَكُمْ﴾ — its meaning, and Allah knows best, is: ”وَواللَّهِ لَأكِيدَنَّ“ ("by Allah, I will surely plot"). The tāʾ of the oath is proper only with ”اَللَّهِ“: you say ”وَحَقِّ اللَّهِ لَأفْعَلَنَّ“ ("by the right of Allah, I will surely do it"), but ”تَحَقِّ اللَّهِ لَأفْعَلَنَّ“ is not permissible; and you say ”وَحَقِّ زَيْدٍ لَأفْعَلَنَّ“. The tāʾ is a substitute for the wāw. ”وَبِاللَّهِ لِأكِيدَنَّ أصْنامَكُمْ“ is also permissible. The reading of the people of the [major] cities is ”تاللَّهِ“; we know of no one among the people of the cities who read it with the bāʾ, though its meaning is sound and good.

zajjaj:58-58.t:
And His words: ﴿فَجَعَلَهم جُذاذًا﴾ — also ”جِذاذًا“; it is read with the ḍamma and the kasra. Whoever reads ”جُذاذًا“: the pattern of everything broken and cut up is ”فُعالٌ“, as in ”اَلْجُذاذُ“ (fragments), ”اَلْحُطامُ“ (debris) and ”اَلرُّفاتُ“ (crumbled remains). Whoever says ”جِذاذًا“, it is the plural of ”جَذِيذٌ“, [singular] ”جَذِيذٌ“ and [plural] ”جِذاذٌ“, like ”ثَقِيلٌ“ / ”ثِقالٌ“ (heavy) and ”خَفِيفٌ“ / ”خِفافٌ“ (light). ”جَذاذًا“ is also permissible, in the sense of ”اَلْقَطاعُ“ (cutting time) and ”اَلْحَصادُ“ (harvest); and ”جُذُذًا“ is permissible, as [the plural of] ”جَذِيدٌ“: ”جُذُذٌ“, like ”جَدِيدٌ“ / ”جُدُدٌ“ (new).
And His words: ﴿إلا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ﴾, i.e. he broke these idols except the biggest of them. It may be that it was the biggest in their eyes, in their veneration of it, not in physical form; and it may be that it was the largest of them in form. The meaning of ”لَعَلَّهم إلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ“ is: ”لَعَلَّهم بِاحْتِجاجِ إبْراهِيمَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِهِ يَرْجِعُونَ، فَيَعْلَمُونَ وُجُوبَ الحُجَّةِ عَلَيْهِمْ“ ("perhaps, through Ibrāhīm's arguing against them by means of it, they would come back and know that the proof was binding upon them").

zajjaj:60-60.t: His words: ﴿قالُوا سَمِعْنا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهم يُقالُ لَهُ إبْراهِيمُ﴾, i.e. he mentions them disparagingly. They said of the idols ”يَذْكُرُهُمْ“ (with the pronoun of rational beings) because in their worship of them they treated them as beings that have reason. ”إبْراهِيمُ“ is nominative in two ways: one in the sense of ”يُقالُ لَهُ: هو إبْراهِيمُ“ ("it is said of him: he is Ibrāhīm") and ”اَلْمَعْرُوفُ بِهِ إبْراهِيمُ“ ("the one known by it is Ibrāhīm"); and as a vocative, in the sense of ”يُقالُ لَهُ: يا إبْراهِيمُ“ ("he is addressed: O Ibrāhīm").

zajjaj:61-61.t: ﴿قالُوا فَأْتُوا بِهِ عَلى أعْيُنِ النّاسِ لَعَلَّهم يَشْهَدُونَ﴾, i.e. perhaps they will recognize him by this saying and bear witness against him, so that what we inflict on him will be on the basis of a proof against him. It is also possible that it means: ”لَعَلَّهم يَشْهَدُونَ عُقُوبَتَنا إيّاهُ“ ("perhaps they will witness our punishment of him").

zajjaj:65-65.t: And His words: ﴿ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا عَلى رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that bewilderment overtook the people. The meaning of ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما هَؤُلاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ is: ”ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا عَلى رُؤُوسِهِمْ فَقالُوا لِإبْراهِيمَ - عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ -: لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما هَؤُلاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ“ ("then they were turned over on their heads and said to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him: you know well that these do not speak"). So they had acknowledged the inability of what they worship to speak.

zajjaj:67-67.t:
And His words: ﴿أُفٍّ لَكم ولِما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — it is read ”أُفِّ لَكُمْ“ without tanwīn and ”أُفٍّ“ with tanwīn. ”أُفٌّ لَكُمْ“ and ”أُفُّ لَكُمْ“ are also permissible, with the ḍamma, with and without tanwīn; and ”أُفَّ لَكُمْ“ with the fatḥa is permissible.
As for the kasra without tanwīn, it is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the two fāʾs in His saying ”أُفِّ“; the basic state of the word is quiescence, because it is in the category of sounds [interjections]. The tanwīn is dropped because it is definite and is not required to be declined. Its interpretation is: ”اَلنُّتْنُ لَكُمْ، ولِما تَعْبُدُونَ“ ("the stench be upon you and upon what you worship"). Whoever gives it tanwīn makes it indefinite, equivalent to ”نُتْنًا لَكم ولِما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ“ ("a stench upon you and upon what you worship besides Allah"). It takes the kasra because the basic vowel for the meeting of two quiescent letters is the kasra, and because most sound-words are indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, as in ”غاقِ“, ”جَيْرِ“, ”أمْسِ“ and ”إيهِ“. The fatḥa is permissible for the meeting of two quiescent letters because of the heaviness of the doubling with the kasra; and the ḍamma is permissible because of the ḍamma of the alif [i.e. the initial hamza], just as they said ”رُدَّ يا هَذا“ ("give it back, you"), ”رُدُّ“ and ”رُدِّ“ with the kasra. Whoever uses tanwīn with the ḍamma treats it like the tanwīn with the kasra.

zajjaj:71-71.t: And His words: ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهُ ولُوطًا إلى الأرْضِ الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that it was [the journey] from the land of Syria (al-Shām) to Iraq. [Translator's note: the text reads «مِن أرْضِ الشّامِ إلى العِراقِ»; the usual account is the reverse, from Iraq to Syria. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:72-72.t: His words: ﴿وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ إسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ نافِلَةً﴾ — ”اَلنّافِلَةُ“ here is the child's child (grandchild), meaning Yaʿqūb specifically.

zajjaj:73-73.t: And His words: ﴿وَإقامَ الصَّلاةِ﴾ — ”إقامِ“ on its own is rare in the language: you say ”أقَمْتُ، إقامَةً“; but ”إقامُ الصَّلاةِ“ is permissible, because the annexation (iḍāfa) compensates for the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa].

zajjaj:74-74.t: And His words: ﴿وَلُوطًا آتَيْناهُ حُكْمًا وعِلْمًا﴾ — ”لُوطًا“ is accusative by an implied verb, because a verb precedes it; so the meaning is: ”وَأوْحَيْنا إلَيْهِمْ، وآتَيْنا لُوطًا آتَيْناهُ حُكْمًا وعِلْمًا“ ("We revealed to them, and We gave Lūṭ — We gave him judgement and knowledge"). The accusative here is better than the nominative, because before ”آتَيْنا“ there is a verb. Some of the grammarians mentioned that it is accusative by ”واذْكُرْ لُوطًا“ ("and mention Lūṭ"), and this is permissible, since mention of Ibrāhīm has gone before, so ”لُوطًا“ was construed in the sense of ”واذْكُرْ“.

zajjaj:76-76.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُوحًا إذْ نادى مِن قَبْلُ فاسْتَجَبْنا لَهُ﴾ — [”نُوحًا“] is accusative by ”واذْكُرْ“ ("and mention").

zajjaj:78-78.t:
Likewise His words: ﴿وَداوُدَ وسُلَيْمانَ إذْ يَحْكُمانِ في الحَرْثِ﴾, in the sense of ”واذْكُرْ داوُدَ وسُلَيْمانَ إذْ يَحْكُمانِ في الحَرْثِ“ ("and mention Dāwūd and Sulaymān when they gave judgement concerning the tillage"). ﴿إذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ القَوْمِ﴾ — ”اَلنَّفْشُ“ is [grazing unattended] by night, and ”اَلْهَمَلُ“ is by day.
It has come in the exegesis that some sheep in the time of Dāwūd and Sulaymān passed by a people's tillage and ruined it. It is related that the tillage was wheat, and it is related that it was a vineyard. They ruined that tillage, and Dāwūd judged that the sheep be handed over to the owners of the vineyard; Sulaymān judged that the sheep be handed over to the owners of the vineyard so that they could take their benefits — their milk, their wool and their ʿawāriḍ — until the vineyard returned to the state it had been in when it was ruined; then, when the vineyard had returned to its state, the sheep would be returned to their owners and the vineyard handed back to the owner of the vineyard. [Translator's note: the text says «ويُدْفَعَ الكَرْمُ إلى صاحِبِ الكَرْمِ»; in the usual account the owners of the sheep tend the vineyard meanwhile, so «صاحِبِ الغَنَمِ» may be intended in an earlier step. Translated as written.]
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: ”عَوارِضَها“ may be taken in one of two ways: either it is the plural of ”عَرِيضٌ“ — also [plural] ”عُرْضانٌ“ — which is a name for the young lamb, mostly used of the young goat; or it may refer to whatever benefits of them present themselves, until the vineyard returns to how it was. This — and Allah knows best — indicates that Sulaymān knew that the value of what the sheep had ruined of the vineyard was equal to the amount of the sheep's yield.

zajjaj:79-79.t:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَفَهَّمْناها سُلَيْمانَ﴾, i.e. We made him understand the case and the judgement. ﴿وَكُلا آتَيْنا حُكْمًا وعِلْمًا﴾.
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ والطَّيْرَ﴾ — ”والطَّيْرُ“ is also permissible, conjoined to [the pronoun] in ”يُسَبِّحْنَ“, but I know of no one who read it so. ﴿وَكُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾, i.e. We were able to do what We willed. ”اَلطَّيْرَ“ is accusative from two angles: one in the sense of ”وَسَخَّرْنا الطَّيْرَ“ ("and We subjected the birds"), and the other in the sense of ”يُسَبِّحْنَ مَعَ الطَّيْرِ“ ("they glorify along with the birds") [as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment)].

zajjaj:80-80.t:
And His words: ﴿وَعَلَّمْناهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَكم لِتُحْصِنَكم مِن بَأْسِكُمْ﴾ — it has also been read ”لِنُحْصِنَكم مِن بَأْسِكُمْ“ with the nūn, and ”لِيُحْصِنَكُمْ“ with the yāʾ is permissible. Whoever reads with the yāʾ means: so that this garment may protect you; it may also be in the sense of: so that Allah may protect you from your violence, and that is like ”لِنُحْصِنَكُمْ“ with the nūn. Whoever reads with the tāʾ means ”لِتُحْصِنَكُمُ الصَّنْعَةُ“ ("so that the craft may protect you"). These three forms have all been read. Three more are permissible in it which have not been read, and they ought not to be read, because reading is a sunna [followed practice]: ”لِنُحَصِّنَكُمْ“ with the nūn and doubling, ”لِتُحَصِّنَكُمْ“ with the tāʾ and doubling, and ”لِيُحَصِّنَكُمْ“ with the yāʾ — with a doubled ṣād in these three.
Allah taught Dāwūd the craft of making coats of mail from chain links; they had not existed before Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and they combined lightness with protection — so it has been related.

zajjaj:81-81.t: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ عاصِفَةً﴾ — it has also been read ”اَلرِّياحَ عاصِفَةً“, and ”اَلرِّيحُ عاصِفَةً“ with ”اَلرِّيحَ“ in the nominative. Whoever reads ”اَلرِّيحَ عاصِفَةً“ in the accusative, it is conjoined to ”اَلْجِبالَ“, and the meaning is: ”وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ، وسَخَّرْنا لِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ“ ("We subjected the mountains along with Dāwūd, and We subjected the wind to Sulaymān"); ”عاصِفَةً“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Whoever reads ”اَلرِّيحُ“ puts it in the nominative, as you say ”لِزَيْدٍ المالُ“ ("to Zayd belongs the wealth"); and this falls within the meaning of subjection, because when He says ”تَجْرِي بِأمْرِهِ إلى الأرْضِ“ ("it flowed by his command to the land"), there is in the speech evidence that Allah, exalted be His praise, subjected it.

zajjaj:82-82.t:
And His words: ﴿وَمِنَ الشَّياطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ﴾ — the position of ”مَن“ may be accusative, conjoined to ”اَلرِّيحَ“. ”مَن“ may also be in the position of the nominative from two angles: one is conjunction with ”اَلرِّيحُ“, the meaning being: ”وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحُ، ولَهُ مَن يَغُوصُونَ مِنَ الشَّياطِينِ“ ("to Sulaymān belonged the wind, and to him belonged those of the devils who dived"); and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with ”لَهُ“ as the khabar (predicate).
And His words: ﴿وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ — its meaning is ”سِوى ذَلِكَ“ ("other than that"), i.e. ”سِوى الغَوْصِ“ ("other than diving"). ﴿وَكُنّا لَهم حافِظِينَ﴾ — Allah guarded them from spoiling what they had made.

zajjaj:83-83.t: And His words: ﴿وَأيُّوبَ إذْ نادى رَبَّهُ﴾ — ”أيُّوبَ“ is accusative in the sense of ”واذْكُرْ أيُّوبَ“ ("and mention Ayyūb").

zajjaj:84-84.t: And His words: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ أهْلَهُ ومِثْلَهم مَعَهُمْ﴾ — most of the interpretations are that Allah, exalted be His praise, brought back to life those of his sons and daughters who had died, and granted him the like of them in children. It was also said: ”آتَيْناهُ أهْلَهُ ومِثْلَهم مَعَهُمْ“ — We will give him [this] in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:85-85.t: ﴿وَإسْماعِيلَ وإدْرِيسَ وذا الكِفْلِ﴾ — all of this is accusative by ”واذْكُرْ“ ("and mention"). It is said that Dhū l-Kifl was given this name because he took responsibility (takaffala) for the affair of a prophet among his community, and carried out what was due concerning them and him. It is also said that he undertook the work of a righteous man and carried it out. ”اَلْكِفْلُ“ in the language is the cloth placed behind the saddle on the camel's rump; and ”اَلْكِفْلُ“ is also said to mean a share. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يُؤْتِكم كِفْلَيْنِ مِن رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 28].

zajjaj:87-87.t:
And His words: ﴿وَذا النُّونِ إذْ ذَهَبَ مُغاضِبًا﴾ — ”ذا النُّونِ“ is Yūnus (Jonah), and ”اَلنُّونُ“ is the fish; the meaning is: ”واذْكُرْ ذا النُّونِ“ ("and mention Dhū l-Nūn"). It is related that he went off angry with his people, and it was said that he went off angry with one of the kings.
﴿فَظَنَّ أنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. he thought that We would not decree for him what We did decree, namely his being in the belly of the whale; ”يَقْدِرُ“ has the meaning of ”يُقَدِّرُ“ ("decrees"), and this has come in the exegesis. It is related from al-Ḥasan that he said: a servant who ran away from his Lord. The interpretation of al-Ḥasan's statement is that he fled from the punishment of his Lord — not that Yūnus thought that flight would save him from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, or from His decree.
And His words: ﴿فَنادى في الظُّلُماتِ أنْ لا إلَهَ إلا أنْتَ﴾ — regarding ”اَلظُّلُماتِ“ there are two views. One is that by it is meant the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea and the darkness of the whale's belly. It may also be that "he called out in the darknesses" means that most of his supplication and calling was in the darknesses of the night. The first interpretation is better, because in the belly of the whale I do not suppose he could distinguish between the darkness of night and other darkness; rather, the first thing he met was the darkness of the night, then the darkness of the sea, then the darkness of the whale's belly. It is also possible that the darknesses coincided at one time, so that the darkness of the whale's belly, at night and in the sea, was the utmost in intensity.

zajjaj:88-88.t: And His words: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُنْجِي المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — what is in the muṣḥaf was written with a single nūn, because the second nūn is concealed [in pronunciation] before the jīm. As for what is related from ʿĀṣim with a single nūn [”نُجِّي“], it is a solecism (laḥn) with no justification, because a verb whose agent is not named cannot be without a [deputy] agent. Some said [it means]: ”نُجِّيَ النَّجاءُ المُؤْمِنِينَ“ ("the saving saved the believers"), but this is an error by the consensus of all the grammarians: ”ضُرِبَ زَيْدًا“ is not permissible meaning ”ضُرِبَ الضَّرْبُ زَيْدًا“ ("the beating was beaten upon Zayd"), because when you say ”ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ“ ("Zayd was beaten") it is already known that what struck him was a beating, so there is no point in implying it and setting it up in place of the agent. The report of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh of his reading ”نُجِّيَ المُؤْمِنِينَ“ contradicts the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ”نُنْجِي“ with two nūns.

zajjaj:90-90.t:
And His words: ﴿وَأصْلَحْنا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ﴾ — it is related that she was barren and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made her fertile; and it is related that there was some ill in her character, and Allah rectified that and made her character good.
And His words: ﴿وَيَدْعُونَنا رَغَبًا ورَهَبًا﴾ — it has also been read ”رَغْبًا ورَهْبًا“; ”اَلرَّغْبُ“ and ”اَلرَّهْبُ“ are two maṣdars (verbal nouns). ”رُغْبًا ورُهْبًا“ is also permissible, but I know of no one who read them — I mean ”اَلرُّغْبُ“ and ”اَلرُّهْبُ“ — in this place. ”اَلرُّغْبُ“ and ”اَلرَّغَبُ“ are like ”اَلْبُخْلُ“ and ”اَلْبَخْلُ“ (miserliness), and ”اَلرُّشْدُ“ and ”اَلرَّشَدُ“ (right guidance).

zajjaj:91-91.t:
And His words: ﴿والَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾ — ”اَلَّتِي“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: ”واذْكُرِ الَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها“ ("and mention her who guarded her chastity"). It is related in some of the exegesis that it means the opening of her garment.
﴿وَجَعَلْناها وابْنَها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ — had ”آيَتَيْنِ“ ("two signs") been said, it would have been sound; but since their case was one, and the sign in both of them together was in meaning a single sign, namely birth without a male, it was permissible to say ”آيَةً“ ("a sign").

zajjaj:92-92.t:
And His words: ﴿إنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ — ”أُمَّتُكُمْ“ is nominative, the khabar (predicate) of ”هَذِهِ“; the meaning is: ”إنَّ هَذِهِ أمَتُّكم في حالِ اجْتِماعِها عَلى الحَقِّ، فَإذا افْتَرَقَتْ فَلَيْسَ مَن خالَفَ الحَقَّ داخِلًا فِيها“ ("this is your community while it is united upon the truth; when it splits, whoever opposes the truth is not included in it"). [Translator's note: ”أمَتُّكم“ is so printed; ”أُمَّتُكم“ is clearly meant.] It is also read ”أمَّةٌ واحِدَةٌ“, as a khabar after a khabar, and its meaning is: ”إنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّةٌ واحِدَةٌ، لَيْسَتْ أُمَمًا“ ("this is one community, not [several] communities"). The accusative of ”أُمَّتُكُمْ“ is also permissible, in the sense of tawkīd (emphasis): ”قِيلَ: إنَّ أُمَّتَكم كُلَّها أُمَّةٌ واحِدَةٌ“ ("it was said: your community, all of it, is one community"). [Translator's note: as printed; the accusative example given puts ”أُمَّتَكم“ after ”إنَّ“ rather than illustrating the tawkīd construction.]
And His words: ﴿وَأنا رَبُّكم فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ ﴿وَتَقَطَّعُوا أمْرَهم بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 93] — the meaning is that Allah informed them that the matter of the proof is one, and that they split apart, because their cutting up of their affair among themselves is division.

zajjaj:94-94.t: And His words: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصّالِحاتِ وهو مُؤْمِنٌ فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ وإنّا لَهُ كاتِبُونَ﴾ — ”كُفْرانَ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like ”اَلْغُفْرانُ“ and ”اَلشُّكْرانُ“. The Arabs say: ”غُفْرانَكَ لا كُفْرانَكَ“ ("[we ask] Your forgiveness, not [we commit] ingratitude to You").

zajjaj:95-95.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحَرامٌ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ أهْلَكْناها أنَّهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ — it has been read ”حِرْمٌ“ and ”حَرامٌ“, and these two are the most common readings; it has also been read ”حَرُمَ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ“ and ”حَرِمَ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ“. It has come in the exegesis that ”حِرْمٌ“ is in the sense of ”حَتْمٌ“ ("decreed"). It has also come from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ”حَتْمٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ألّا يُرْجَعُوا إلى دُنْياهُمْ“ ("it is decreed for them that they will not be returned to their worldly life"), and it has come from him [as well]. [Translator's note: the sentence «وجاءَ عَنْهُ» breaks off here in the text.]
And from Qatāda: that they will not return to repentance. According to the lexicographers, ”حِرْمٌ“ and ”حَرامٌ“ have one meaning, like ”حِلٌّ“ and ”حَلالٌ“ ("lawful"). The apparent sense of ”حَرامٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أنَّهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ“ ("it is forbidden to them that they do not return") needs to be explained, and I know of no one among the lexicographers or the exegetes who has explained it. It is — and Allah knows best — that when He said: ﴿فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ وإنّا لَهُ كاتِبُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 94], He informed us that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has forbidden the acceptance of the deeds of the disbelievers, and He made that clear by His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1]. So the meaning is: ”حَرامٌ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ أهْلَكْناها أنْ نَتَقَبَّلَ مِنهم عَمَلًا، لِأنَّهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ“ ("it is forbidden for a town We have destroyed that We should accept any deed from them, because they do not return"), i.e. ”لا يَتُوبُونَ“ ("they do not repent"). ”حَرِمَ“ and ”حَرُمَ“ are in the sense of ”حَرامٌ“, except that ”حَرامٌ“ is a noun, while ”حَرِمَ“ and ”حَرُمَ“ are verbs.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
And His words: ﴿حَتّى إذا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ ومَأْجُوجُ﴾ — with a hamza and without a hamza. They are two tribes of Allah's creation. It is related that mankind is ten parts, nine of which are Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj (Gog and Magog). They are two non-Arab names; the derivation of their like from the speech of the Arabs would be taken from ”أجَّجْتُ النّارَ“ ("I kindled the fire") and from ”اَلْماءُ الأُجاجُ“ ("bitter water") — which is more intense: it is water of extreme saltiness, burning from its saltiness.
And His words: ﴿وَهم مِن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ — it has also been transmitted as ”مِن كُلِّ جَدَثٍ يَنْسِلُونَ“ ("from every grave"), with the jīm and the thāʾ; but the better in this word is ”حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ“ with the ḥāʾ. ”اَلْحَدَبُ“ is every hillock, and ”يَنْسِلُونَ“ means "they hasten".

zajjaj:97-97.t: And His words: ﴿واقْتَرَبَ الوَعْدُ الحَقُّ فَإذا هي شاخِصَةٌ﴾ — some said the sense of the wāw is that it is to be dropped [i.e. redundant (zāʾida)]. The apodosis (jawāb) according to the Basrans is His saying: ﴿يا ويْلَنا قَدْ كُنّا في غَفْلَةٍ مِن هَذا﴾, and here there is an omitted "saying"; the meaning is: ”حَتّى إذا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ ومَأْجُوجُ واقْتَرَبَ الوَعْدُ الحَقُّ قالُوا: يا ويْلَنا قَدْ كُنّا في غَفْلَةٍ مِن هَذا بَلْ كُنّا ظالِمِينَ“ ("until, when Gog and Magog are let loose and the true promise draws near, they will say: woe to us, we were heedless of this; rather we were wrongdoers"). It has come in the exegesis that the emergence of Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj is one of the signs of the Hour.

zajjaj:98-98.t: His words: ﴿إنَّكم وما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ — it has been read in three ways: ”حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ“, ”حَطَبُ جَهَنَّمَ“ and ”حَضَبُ جَهَنَّمَ“ with the dotted ḍād. Whoever reads ”حَصَبُ“, its meaning is: everything thrown into Hell. Whoever says ”حَطَبُ“, its meaning is: what Hell is kindled with (firewood), as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقُودُها النّاسُ والحِجارَةُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 6]. Whoever says ”حَضَبُ“ with the dotted ḍād, its meaning is: that by which the fire is stirred up and made to blaze; and ”اَلْحَضْبُ“ is the snake.

zajjaj:104-104.t:
And His words: ﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ﴾ — also ”لِلْكِتابِ“. It is also read ”اَلسِّجْلُ“ with the lām undoubled; whoever lightens it gives the jīm a sukūn. It has come in the exegesis that al-sijill is the scroll on which the writing is. It was said that al-sijill is an angel; and it was said that al-sijill, in the language of the army, is "the man". [Translator's note: «بِلُغَةِ الجَيْشِ» is as printed; «بِلُغَةِ الحَبَشِ» ("in the language of the Abyssinians") is probably intended.] It is reported from Abū l-Jawzāʾ that al-Sijill was a scribe of the Prophet ﷺ. The sentence is completed at ”لِلْكُتُبِ“.
And His words: ﴿كَما بَدَأْنا أوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ﴾ is resumptive (mustaʾnaf); the meaning is: ”نَبْعَثُ الخَلْقَ كَما بَدَأْناهُمْ“ ("We will raise creation as We began them"), i.e. ”قُدْرَتُنا عَلى الإعادَةِ كَقُدْرَتِنا عَلى الِابْتِداءِ“ ("Our power to bring back is like Our power to originate"). ”يَوْمَ تُطْوى السَّماءُ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ“ is permissible, and ”يَوْمَ يَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ“ is permissible, but ”يَطْوِي“ has not been read; what has been read is ”نَطْوِي“ and ”تُطْوى“, with the nūn and the tāʾ.
And His words: ﴿وَعْدًا عَلَيْنا﴾ — ”وَعْدًا“ is accusative as a maṣdar [mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], because His saying ”نُعِيدُهُ“ has the sense of ”وَعَدْنا هَذا وعْدًا“ ("We have promised this as a promise").
And His words: ﴿إنّا كُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾, i.e. able to do whatever We will.

zajjaj:105-105.t:
And His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنا في الزَّبُورِ مِن بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ﴾ — ”اَلزَّبُورُ“ is all the scriptures: the Torah, the Gospel and the Furqān are each a zabūr, because ”اَلزَّبُورُ“ and ”اَلْكِتابُ“ have one meaning; one says ”زَبَرْتُ“ and ”كَتَبْتُ“ ("I wrote") with one meaning. The meaning is: ”وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنا في الكُتُبِ مِن بَعْدِ ذِكْرِنا في السَّماءِ“ ("We have written in the scriptures after Our record in heaven").
﴿أنَّ الأرْضَ يَرِثُها عِبادِيَ الصّالِحُونَ﴾ — it was said in the exegesis that it is the land of Paradise, and the evidence for this view is His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الوارِثُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 10] ﴿الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الفِرْدَوْسَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 11].
It was also said that by "the earth" here is meant the earth of this world, and this view is more likely, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 1]; when ”اَلْأرْضُ“ is mentioned, it indicates the earth that we know. Further evidence for this view is His saying: ﴿وَأوْرَثْنا القَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشارِقَ الأرْضِ ومَغارِبَها الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 137]. This verse is among the most important proof-texts of the jurists that land is not treated in the same way as other things that are developed.

zajjaj:108-108.t: And His words: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما يُوحى إلَيَّ أنَّما إلَهُكم إلَهٌ واحِدٌ﴾ — the better is ”أنَّما إلَهُكُمْ“ with a fatḥa on ”أنَّ“, and that is the reading. If it were read ”إنَّما“, it would be permissible, because the meaning of ”يُوحى إلَيَّ“ is ”يُقالُ لِي“ ("it is said to me"); but the reading is the fatḥa and nothing else.

zajjaj:109-109.t: And His words: ﴿فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكم عَلى سَواءٍ﴾ — ”آذَنْتُكُمْ“: I have informed you of what is revealed to me, so that you may be equal in believing in it.

zajjaj:111-111.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ أدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ لَكم ومَتاعٌ إلى حِينٍ﴾, i.e. ”وَما أدْرِي ما آذَنْتُكم بِهِ فِتْنَةٌ لَكُمْ“ ("and I do not know [whether] what I have informed you of is a trial for you"), i.e. a test for you.

zajjaj:112-112.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ احْكم بِالحَقِّ﴾ — it is also read ”قُلْ رَبِّ احْكم بِالحَقِّ“, and it is permissible — and it has been read so — ”قالَ رَبِّيَ احْكم بِالحَقِّ“. The messengers who passed before used to say: ”رَبَّنا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالحَقِّ“ ("our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth"), and its meaning is "judge"; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded His Prophet to say: ”رَبِّ احْكم بِالحَقِّ“ ("my Lord, judge in truth").
And His words: ﴿وَرَبُّنا الرَّحْمَنُ المُسْتَعانُ عَلى ما تَصِفُونَ﴾, i.e. against the lies you tell.
